subject: Request: temporary SLO variance for embedder-preview launch
messages:
From: Eva Morris <eva@gaia.ai>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Cc: Bryan Lee <bryan.lee@gaia.ai>
Date: Fri, 1 Oct 2026 15:22:00 -0700
Subject: Request: temporary SLO variance for embedder-preview launch

Hi Vivek / Marissa,

We're planning to open a preview for our new contextual embedder (v2-preview) next week and expect an initial burst of traffic from internal search/recall tests and a small set of early partners. The embedder improves semantic recall but has substantially higher token-side compute in the first 2-3 tokens due to a new pre-normalization step — we've seen 99th percentile latencies in our staging runs around ~420–480ms on the instance types you've recommended.

Because this is a preview, our product team is comfortable with a temporary relaxation of the latency SLO for the model, but procurement/legal asked that we get a documented exception from Redwood so we can proceed without opening a formal outage ticket. Specifically, we need:
- A formal exception that applies only to model_name=embedder-v2-preview and model_version=2026-10-01-preview
- A guaranteed window (start/end) and a clear rollback trigger if production impact is seen
- Audit logs and any guardrails you can apply so downstream services don't see timeouts unexpectedly

Can you confirm whether Redwood can support a temporary 99th-percentile latency SLO of 500ms for a 3-week preview window (target window: Oct 8 -> Oct 29) and what operational controls you recommend? Also please list any attachments or run logs you'd like from our side.

Thanks —
Eva
Eva Morris
Head of AI, Gaia AI
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>
To: Eva Morris <eva@gaia.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 1 Oct 2026 16:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: temporary SLO variance for embedder-preview launch

Eva — thanks for the clear ask. We can support this, but need to align on operational constraints and a short playbook for rollback. Immediate next steps from our side:
1) Loop in Karthik to propose the exception window & mitigations (rate caps, canary routing).
2) Marissa will prepare the formal exception doc for signatures and legal.
3) We will need your staging run logs and a short traffic profile (QPS, percent of calls that are long-running) so our infra team can size/limit correctly.

Karthik — can you propose specific SLO parameters and the guardrail list (logging/threshold alerts) so we can confirm by Monday? Laura — please put this on the queue for the exception template review.

Vivek
VP, Sales Engineering
Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Cc: Eva Morris <eva@gaia.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 4 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: temporary SLO variance for embedder-preview launch

Team — dug into the staging traces you sent (thanks, Eva). Proposed approach below. High level: we can grant a timebound SLO variance for embedder-v2-preview with strict mitigations to limit blast radius.

Proposed exception parameters:
- Scope: model_name=embedder-v2-preview, model_version=2026-10-01-preview (explicitly pinned)
- Window: 2026-10-08T00:00:00Z -> 2026-10-29T23:59:59Z (21 days)
- SLO for window: 99th percentile latency ≤ 500ms (measured at the API ingress per-customer token request)
- Throughput cap: soft QPS cap (customer-level) of 45 QPS for the preview tag; hard cap at 75 QPS to prevent queue buildup
- Fallback: automatic reroute to embedder-v1 (stable) if 5-minute rolling error rate > 2% or 99th latency > 700ms

Guardrails and telemetry:
- Continuous tracing enabled for all preview requests; retention of traces for 30 days
- Real-time alerting to oncall infra when 99th latency breaches 450ms for >5 minutes
- Prefix/KV cache will be enabled where possible for repeated calls (saves ~30% p99)
- Rate-limiting applied at the customer token key with a 10% traffic buffer for canary experiments

Attachments I'm including: preview-run-logs.zip (staging traces you provided, annotated), slo-exception-mplan.pdf (operational playbook + rollback steps). Please confirm the window and that procurement is happy with the limited-scope nature.

--
Karthik Iyer
Principal Infra Engineer, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference
